response.title: which solar generator is best for an rv with a 30 amp plug
response.answer:
For an RV with a 30-amp shore power plug (TT-30), I'd recommend a solar generator with at least 3,600W of continuous AC output, a native 30A RV outlet, and expandable battery capacity.

The important distinction is that a 30-amp RV connection can supply up to 3,600 watts at 120V. Many portable solar generators have large batteries but can't deliver enough power to run an RV's air conditioner, microwave, and other appliances together.

My top choices are the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, Anker SOLIX F3800, and BLUETTI AC500 with B300S batteries. They serve somewhat different needs.

Native TT-30 RV outlet, no adapter required. Expandable battery, up to 2,600W solar input, and strong air-conditioner compatibility.

Best for powering your entire RV through its shore-power cord.

Official specifications

BLUETTI Apex 300

2,764.8Wh battery · 3,840W output

Native 30A TT-30 outlet with 3,600W maximum through that outlet. Expandable storage.

Good alternative for full 30A RV power with a smaller starting battery.

Shop

Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus

3,840Wh battery · 6,000W total output

Native TT-30 RV outlet, but that outlet is limited to approximately 3,000W rather than the full 3,600W.

Best to consider if you also want substantial home backup capability.

How long will it run your RV?

Using the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3's 4,096Wh battery, these are approximate runtimes before recharging, assuming 85% usable AC energy.

## How long will it run your RV?

Using the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3's 4,096Wh battery, these are approximate runtimes before recharging, assuming 85% usable AC energy.

| RV power consumption | Estimated runtime |
|---|---:|
| 150W — lights, fridge, electronics | 23 hours |
| 500W — moderate use | 7 hours |
| 1,200W — rooftop AC running | 2.9 hours |
| 1,800W — heavier AC load | 1.9 hours |

Actual runtimes vary with compressor cycling, appliance loads, and temperature. Solar panels can extend these times, but 400–800W of portable solar generally won't continuously offset a rooftop air conditioner.
